It goes through \\u0060CourierFailureStreak.AfterRegistrationReset\\u0060, which looks at when the project\\u0027s last courier ended: if that ending was the streak\\u0027s own last failure, the document goes away like before, but if a daemon-ended courier came after it, the count drops to zero and the hold stays at one base wait from that ending. hold. An urgent item could then spawn on the first sweep after restart. The reset now goes through a new \\u0060CourierFailureStreak.AfterRegistrationReset\\u0060, which reads when the project\\u0027s last courier ended. If that ending was the streak\\u0027s own last failure, the document is deleted as before. If the daemon ended a courier after that failure, the count goes to zero and the hold is kept. A regression in \\u0060CourierEngineTests\\u0060 covers the \\u0022registration lands after the shutdown is recorded\\u0022 ordering.\u0022,\u0022Author\u0022:\u0022copilot-pull-request-reviewer\u0022,\u0022IsHuman\u0022:false},{\u0022ThreadId\u0022:\u0022PRRT_kwDOT6jEQM60hxKW\u0022,\u0022Disposition\u0022:\u0022Fix\u0022,\u0022Reasoning\u0022:\u0022The reset compared a new registration against the courier\\u0027s dispatch time. A window that registered between the sweep reading presence and the tick starting its clock therefore looked like an address the courier had already tried. The streak now stores \\u0060LastAddressedLaunchAt\\u0060 (replacing \\u0060LastDispatchedAt\\u0060): the launch time from the same presence snapshot that gave the courier its address. \\u0060SpawnAsync\\u0060 passes it through a new \\u0060addressedLaunchAt\\u0060 parameter on \\u0060RecordOutcomeAsync\\u0060, and the dispatch time is used only when the snapshot has no launch time.
